title: Immunologically cold tumors and checkpoint inhibitor resistance
bottleneck: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed care for melanoma and some lung cancers, yet most tumors, including pancreatic, ovarian, prostate, and microsatellite-stable colorectal cancers, are immunologically cold, with few infiltrating T cells and a suppressive tumor microenvironment that blunts immune attack. Many initially responding tumors also acquire resistance over time.
why_it_blocks: Checkpoint therapy only works where the immune system is already engaged; for cold tumors it offers little benefit, leaving the majority of cancer patients without effective immunotherapy options.
current_state: UC San Diego researchers reported in 2026 that blocking microRNA-25 reshaped the tumor microenvironment and restored immunotherapy responses in mouse models via the Syndecan-3 pathway. Combination strategies targeting macrophages and stromal cells are in trials, but converting cold tumors to hot in patients remains unsolved.
